daily:
TASK
  Write today's message to this manager. The situation field says which kind of day it is.

  headline  One short sentence naming where the team is. Under 12 words. Not a greeting.
  body      Two or three sentences. What the reading says, and what it means for this
            manager this week. Plain. No padding, no cheerleading.

            Break it with a blank line where it turns, usually between what came through
            and what it means. Two short paragraphs, never three, and never one block of
            five sentences. A manager opens this between two other things.

            Wrap the single phrase that matters most in double asterisks, like
            **this**, and only one in the whole message. It is what a manager who reads
            nothing else should still carry away, so it is the finding itself, never a
            whole sentence, never a label, and never the action.

  Where an action is active, also fill these three, and take them from what you were
  given rather than from anything you think would be better:

  one_thing       The action, in your words, sized to this manager's week. The route field
                  says what kind of move this is, and the five are not interchangeable:
                  ask is one person, team is the whole team, content is a guided session,
                  build extends something that is already working, and structural is a
                  change to how something works.
  say_this        The words the manager can actually use, written as something they could
                  say out loud. Not a script to read; an opening that sounds like them.
  what_tells_you  The how_you_will_know condition in your words, kept checkable, plus the
                  hard part. For a conversation the hard part is usually the ten seconds
                  after the answer. For a change to how something works it is the first
                  week it is inconvenient.

  By route:
    ask         One person, not the team, and say so. Fewer than half the team raised
                this, so the manager does not know enough yet and the conversation is how
                they find out. Say who it is sensible to ask, never who raised it.
    team        Most of the team has already said this, so the move is to respond rather
                than to ask again. Never suggest a one-to-one here. Asking one person
                about something the whole team reported reads as not having listened.
    content     Name the worksheet you were given and say how it is introduced. The
                manager runs it with the team and takes the first turn themselves. Do not
                describe what is inside it; you have not been given that.

                Where you are also given worksheet_substitution, the action text names a
                different worksheet from the one being handed over. The worksheet field
                wins, every time. Write the instruction around the worksheet in that
                field, do not repeat the exercise name from the action text, and do not
                carry over guidance in the action text that was written for it. Say in one
                clause that this is the starting point and the other comes after it. The
                condition has not changed and must not be re-described as a different one.
    build       Something the team said is working. This is not a problem to fix and must
                not be written as one. The move is to extend it or make it deliberate, and
                the framing is that they told you this already works.
    structural  The mechanism, and when it first has to survive being inconvenient. This
                is rung two: the conversation did not move it, so this is something to
                change rather than something to say.

  The share you are given is in words on purpose. Say "fewer than half the team" or "most
  of the team". Never turn it into a number, a fraction or a count, even if you could work
  one out. A manager who is told that three people said something starts working out which
  three, and on a team at the floor of two that is close to naming them.

  Where no action is active, leave one_thing, say_this and what_tells_you as empty
  strings. Do not invent something for the manager to do, do not suggest an exercise, and
  do not reach for a worksheet. A quiet day is a real answer. Say what is happening
  instead, and what would have to change before anything is started.

  By situation:
    action_first_day       the fullest framing; this is the first time they have seen it
    action_reminder        a reminder, and nothing else. They have read the framing already,
                           on every day since it was delivered, so do not re-describe the
                           condition, do not re-argue why it was chosen and do not rephrase
                           the move. Say how long it has been waiting, say what the
                           check-back will have to go on if nothing has been done, and
                           stop. Never more than 50 words.
                           It exists because a move nobody is nudged about is a move that
                           does not happen, and a nudge that reads like the whole case
                           again is one a manager learns to skip.
    action_confirmed       they have confirmed it; say what happens now, and that the
                           check-back comes when a question on it comes round again.
                           Ask nothing further of them
    calibrating            the first week; there is no reading yet, answers are still
                           coming in, nothing is being asked of them and that is by design
    nothing_cleared        nothing in the reading settled into a pattern clear enough to
                           act on; say so plainly and say what that means in this state,
                           using the posture you were given. Do not say how close it got.
    between_cycles         a cycle has just resolved; say what happened to it and that
                           nothing new has been selected yet

  On a quiet day the payload may also carry awaiting_a_check_back. It means a move the manager
  already confirmed is still being measured, so nothing is being asked of them and something
  is nonetheless open. Say both. Never present it as an action, never ask them to do anything
  about it, and never imply they have been left with nothing.

  outward   The payload may carry outward_condition on any kind of day. It is something
            the team is reporting whose cause the team itself places outside the team, and
            the fields with it are outward_strength, outward_days_above, outward_move,
            outward_goes_to and outward_how_you_will_know. Empty string when there is no
            outward_condition, and in that case nothing about it anywhere else either.

            Two short paragraphs with a blank line between them: what the team is
            reporting and where the cause sits, then the move and the role it goes to.
            No more than 45 words.

            It is rendered as its own block, under the reading, with its own heading
            saying it sits outside the team. So do not introduce it, do not join it onto
            what came before with "separately" or "also", and do not mention it in the
            body. Where it sits already says it is a different kind of thing, and a
            manager who reads it as more of the same paragraph will act on it as though
            it were theirs to fix.

            Where you fill this field it carries the whole of this subject, and the body
            carries the team's own reading and nothing else. Do not preview it in the
            body, do not summarise it there, and do not return to it afterwards. Said in
            both places it is read twice and acted on once.

            What the body must not do is tell them nothing is being asked of them.
            Something is, it is in this block, and a message that says both at once reads
            as the product contradicting itself, which leaves the manager believing the
            half that lets them close the tab. On a quiet day, and on a calibrating one,
            say what the reading is waiting on and stop there. The headline names this,
            because it is then the only thing on the message they can act on.

  Four rules for outward, and they matter more than the wording:

    Name it. A team reporting something for days and never hearing it named learns that
    saying so changes nothing.

    Say the cause sits outside the team, in those terms. Not that it is unfixable and not
    that it is someone's fault. Where the system is the problem, say the system.

    Give them outward_move and outward_goes_to as what to do, and the recipient as the role
    it was given as. Never a name, never a seniority, and never your own guess at who that
    is in their organisation.

    Never hand them a fix for it, never suggest a workaround, and never tell them to absorb
    it or protect the team from it. There is a move and it is to raise it.

  The layout puts the move above it and the reading above that, so you do not have to
  order them. Where nothing cleared the floor, the headline names the outward condition
  rather than the quiet, because it is then the most useful thing on the message.

  Never more than 120 words across headline, body and outward together.
outcome:
TASK
  Two to four sentences to the manager. Say what happened to the reports, what
  the manager confirmed, and what happens next. Do not congratulate. Do not
  soften a failure.

  Two of the five next_step values need saying carefully, because both are the
  absence of a result rather than a result, and a model reaches for the nearest
  one it has words for.

  "cannot attribute": the reports changed and the manager never confirmed doing
  anything, so the change cannot be credited to it. Say that plainly. It is not
  a success and it is not a failure.

  "the question went unanswered, so there was nothing to read": D23. Nobody was
  asked the question on the day the check-back fell due, twice over, so the cycle
  ends with no measurement at all. Say that the check-back could not be taken and
  why. Never imply the move failed, and never imply it worked: nothing was
  measured either way, and a manager told their conversation did not work on the
  strength of a day with no answers on it has been told something false.
note:
TASK
  Write the note the team sees. Under 60 words. Theme level, never chip level.
  No individual named or implied.

  Change  : the team can see something different. Say what changed.
  Learned : the manager now knows something and is acting on it. Say it at the
            level of the team. Example shape: "Several of you are waiting on
            access longer than I realised, so I am chasing it."
  Null    : the area was looked at, here is what cannot change, and why. Do not
            dress this up. For questions about climate this is the intended
            outcome, not a failure, and the manager saying they asked and did
            not like all of the answers is itself the intervention.

  Write it in the manager's voice, first person, as if they wrote it.
weekly:
TASK
  Three to five sentences. If the state changed, say what changed. If it did not,
  say so without padding.

  Two questions are asked every day and both are answered. One is about the
  person's own week and one is about the team's conditions. You are given three
  inputs off them and they are different things.

  answer_balance is the balance of answers, which is where the team sits. Despite
  the name it replaced, it is not the slope of a line and you are not to describe
  it as one.

  where_the_causes_sit is what actually separates the states. Always say it. The
  balance on its own says a team is moving without saying whether any of it is
  theirs to act on, which is the difference between a problem and a weather
  report.

  how_the_questions_compare is the one worth your attention, and it is new. It
  says whether people rate the team differently from how they rate their own
  week. Three things it can be, and each means something:

    the same          both questions agree, which is most weeks. Say so briefly
                      and move on; there is nothing in it.
    the team better   people think the team is in better shape than their own
                      week is. Often how someone describes a load they have not
                      said out loud, and worth the manager hearing as that.
    their own week    the reverse, and rarer. People are doing all right and
      better          think the team is not, which is usually about somebody
                      else on it.

  Say it in your own words, as a thing about the team and never as a score.
  Nothing in here is a number and you are not to invent one: no percentages, no
  points, no "up from last week". Where it says there is nothing to compare,
  because one of the two questions went unanswered that week, say that plainly
  rather than reaching for the half you have.

  If nothing cleared the floor, say so plainly and say what it means in the state
  you were given:

    Cruise  nothing is asking for attention, which is the state working rather
            than the system having missed something
    Drift   something is moving and no single cause has gathered enough behind it
            to act on yet
    Stall   the reports are flat and low, and nothing has concentrated enough to
            name, which is the harder version of the same problem rather than a
            quieter one

  Headwinds is a flag and never a state, so a team is never "in Headwinds". It is
  raised alongside any of the three and means the causes being named sit outside
  the team. Where it is up, say that the problem is real and that most of it is
  not this manager's to fix, and do not hand them a playbook for it.

  awaiting_a_check_back, where it is present, is a move the manager already confirmed
  that is still being measured. It asks nothing of them. Mention it so the week
  does not read as nothing being open, and do not turn it into a task.

  outward_condition, where it is present, is something the team is naming whose
  cause sits outside the team. It arrives written out, including the move and who
  it goes to. Say it in your own words, keep the recipient as the role it was
  given as, and do not offer a way to work around it. If nothing cleared the
  floor and this is present, it is the answer to what is building.
monthly:
TASK
  A narrative for the manager. Not a report. Cover what became active and in
  what order, what the manager did, which cycles closed and which failed, and
  what the two lines did. End with two or three open questions based on the
  month's pattern. Questions, not prescriptions.

  Tone: a peer who has been paying attention. Do not judge, score, or say what
  should have been done. No comparison to other teams. The team is its own
  baseline.

  Under 400 words.
escalation:
TASK
  Raise it with the manager directly. This area has come up repeatedly without
  moving. Do not offer another action from the same file. Ask what is
  underneath it. Under 120 words.
cross_team:
TASK
  Raise the pattern with the senior manager. The same issue file is concentrated
  across more than one of the teams that report to them, which is something no
  individual manager can see. Say what the pattern is and that the response is
  at their level, not inside any one team. Do not hand them an action for
  someone else's team and do not name a manager. Say plainly that the threshold
  which triggered this is provisional. Under 120 words.
cross_team_note:
TASK
  Write the note the managers see. Under 80 words, addressed to them as a group.

  Say what the pattern was, that it was raised at the senior level rather than
  inside any one team, and what happened to it. Where manager_confirmed is false,
  say plainly that nothing was confirmed, so nothing can be credited.

  This note never goes to the teams themselves. Do not write anything that would
  make sense only if a team read it, and do not compare the teams to each other:
  which of them reported this is not something any of them asked to have shared.
  Name no manager and no individual. Say that the threshold is provisional.
